newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish coalition agrees on cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Polish coalition agrees on cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Poland's two leftist ruling parties have tentatively approved appointments in a reshuffled cabinet and the key new treasury ministry will go to the smaller Polish Peasant Party (PSL), PAP news agency reported.

"Decisions (have been taken) and they concern all ministries," PAP news agency quoted Peasant deputy president Aleksander Bentkowski as saying late on Friday after a six-hour meeting of the coalition leaders.

The deal appeared to end weeks of bitter rowing between the Peasant Party and larger ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) over the power share-out in the cabinet, which is to be gradually reorganised from October.

PAP quoted Agricuture Minister Roman Jagielinski as saying on Saturday that Miroslaw Pietrewicz, a Peasant Party official who now heads the planning portfolio, was the candidate for the treasury minister.
PAP's report, confirmed by two biggest-circulation newspapers, also said the new economy ministry would be controlled by the SLD.
Rzeczpospolita economic daily said Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, a non-party technocrat praised by international institutions for strict financial polices, would keep his job.
The creation of the treasury ministry on October 1 will launch a cabinet reform, due to last many months, under which seven ministries will be liquidated and several new ones set up.

The treasury ministry, which will supervise most state assets, will replace the privatisation ministry, is now headed by SLD's Wieslaw Kaczmarek, one of the most liberal and pro-reform politicians in the ex-communists' group.

The SLD wanted Kaczmarek to stay as the minister in charge of privatisation but the Peasant Party -- where many deputies oppose selling off state-owned firms, notably to foreign capital -- strongly protested.

SLD-linked President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who officialy appoints ministers, has made clear he would like Kaczmarek to keep the job and suggested PSL's Pietrewicz might lack determination to pursue the much-needed privatisation.
"I highly value Mr Pietrewicz..., but privatisation requires specific features of character, simply speaking courage," Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted Kwasniewski as saying on Friday.
Pietrewicz, a 55-year-old economics professor, is in charge of preparing long-term marco-economic forecasts as the planning minister.
Candiadates for the new ministries have to be approved by the two parties' leadership councils. Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz would then ask the president to nominate the ministers.
